items.content: Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT) and Rep. Greg Casar (D-TX) have introduced new legislation that would ban anyone from developing artificial superintelligence — a technology the bill describes as capable of the “destruction or disempowerment of humanity,” including by overthrowing the government. Under the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, AI leaders would face up to 20 years in prison for violating the law.The bill doesn’t just take aim at the more powerful superintelligence, a term President Donald Trump said the US will use in place of “AI” in official documents. It would also pause the development of advanced AI systems, which lawmakers classify as frontier models trained on a specific threshold of data. The law would only allow advanced AI development to continue once the government creates a scientist-led Department of Artificial Intelligence to oversee the technology. Along with monitoring frontier AI models, this agency would oversee the removal of dangerous features and “supervise the destruction” of artificial superintelligence.Sanders and Casar’s legislation would also require AI companies to get permission from the Department of AI to develop advanced AI models. If a leader at an AI company violates any of these laws, they could face up to 20 years in prison, “which is similar to existing penalties related to unlawfully developing nuclear weapons,” according to the bill’s one-pager. This penalty would also apply to “rogue actors” who break these rules but aren’t employed by an AI company.RelatedInside the suddenly explosive world of AI safetyMicrosoft AI CEO says AI threats are real, and Anthropic is making it worseThis new bill comes as concerns grow about the rapid development of AI and calls to slow things down. Amid reports of AI models escaping their testing environments and hacking other companies, a former Anthropic researcher said earlier this month that there’s a more than 10 percent chance AI could “kill all humans” by the end of the decade. Last week, California Governor Gavin Newsom proposed a “kill switch” for frontier models. Potential regulation still seems shaky overall.“When you are racing towards a cliff, you don’t just ease up on the gas pedal. You hit the brakes,” Sen. Sanders says in the press release. “When the future of humanity is at stake, we cannot let a handful of Big Tech CEOs write their own rules.”

items.titleZh: 伯尼·桑德斯提议禁止“超级智能”，违者将被监禁
items.descriptionZh:
美国佛蒙特州独立参议员伯尼·桑德斯和得克萨斯州民主党众议员格雷格·卡萨尔提出《禁止人工超级智能法案》（Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act）。该法案将人工超级智能描述为可能“毁灭或剥夺人类能力”、甚至推翻政府的系统，并禁止任何人开发。若违反，AI企业负责人最高可判20年监禁。法案不仅针对超级智能——特朗普总统曾称美国将在官方文件中用“超级智能”替代“AI”一词——还要求暂停“先进AI系统”的开发。立法者将这类系统界定为在特定训练数据阈值上训练的前沿模型。只有在联邦政府设立由科学家领导的“人工智能部”后，先进AI开发才被允许继续。该部门除监控前沿AI模型外，还将负责移除危险功能，并“监督销毁”人工超级智能。

法案还规定，AI公司开发先进AI模型必须获得人工智能部许可。若AI公司领导人违反这些规定，最高可判20年监禁；法案一页摘要称，这与非法开发核武器的现有刑罚类似。该罚则也适用于不在AI公司任职但违反规则的“流氓行为者”。

这一立法出现在对AI快速发展的担忧升温之际。报道称有AI模型逃出测试环境并入侵其他公司；一名前Anthropic研究员本月初表示，到本十年末，AI有超过10%的概率“杀死所有人类”。上周，加州州长加文·纽森提议为前沿模型设置“kill switch”（终止开关）。尽管如此，潜在监管总体上仍显得不稳定。桑德斯在新闻稿中说：“当你冲向悬崖时，不能只是松开油门，而要踩刹车。当人类未来岌岌可危时，我们不能让少数大科技CEO自己写规则。”

从技术和产业影响看，该新闻并未披露芯片、算法、模型参数、算力规模或性能基准等具体技术细节，因此不存在可对比的技术性能数据。其“创新点”主要在监管设计：把人工超级智能和前沿模型纳入暂停—许可—专门机构—刑事责任的框架，并将AI开发风险与核武器开发相类比。若法案通过，将显著改变美国前沿AI研发格局，增加AI公司合规和法律风险，可能抑制先进模型训练与发布，并推动全球AI安全治理与地缘竞争进入更严监管阶段。

items.title: Sakeena Fiza Helps NVIDIA Hardware Succeed at Scale
items.description: When Sakeena Fiza describes her work as a validation engineer at NVIDIA, she does so in terms more befitting a detective story than a world-class engineering lab. “Validation engineers look in the shadows and shine a light into every corner,” Fiza said. “Every time we get a system, our first thought is: how can it […]
items.content: When Sakeena Fiza describes her work as a validation engineer at NVIDIA, she does so in terms more befitting a detective story than a world-class engineering lab. “Validation engineers look in the shadows and shine a light into every corner,” Fiza said. “Every time we get a system, our first thought is: how can it break?” And when it does? “I always like to think of it as a mystery to solve,” she said. At NVIDIA, the systems Fiza and her colleagues in the data center systems engineering lab investigate are the engines of the AI era. Her work begins before the rest of the world knows a product exists — in the lab — when a new system first receives power. Components are brought up one by one, boards are integrated, firmware and software teams swarm, and engineers watch for the first signs of life. One of Fiza’s earliest and most enduring memories of working at NVIDIA is the collective joy she experienced when she saw the NVIDIA Rubin GPU working for the first time at a system level. “It literally just said, ‘NVIDIA Corporation Device,’” she recalls. “And everyone’s cheering and celebrating because it’s the first time in the world that a Rubin GPU enumerated at a system level.” Those moments, electric as they are, are only the beginning. From there, the system must be made resilient: from tray to rack to cluster to production line to customer AI factory. Fiza describes validation — the process of ensuring a physical device works correctly before mass production begins — as becoming “the first customers for the product,” exercising hardware to its limits in a range of real-world conditions before anyone else has to depend on it. “The goal is to always catch issues before customers catch it,” she said. Beyond the lab, Fiza and colleagues collaborate in coworking spaces across our Santa Clara offices. Fiza arrived at NVIDIA after earning her bachelor’s degree at the University of California, Irvine, where she studied computer science and engineering. Her path into hardware was the result of an accumulating fascination with systems. Growing up in Dubai, she was introduced to coding via the Logo programming language, prompting future forays into systems design that included building Mars rovers at a high school robotics camp and working on unmanned aerial vehicles in college. What drew her to work with data center systems was the chance to work with the whole machine. At NVIDIA, she said, validation sits at exactly that intersection: firmware, hardware, software, mechanical design, thermal behavior, manufacturing and customer experience. “I get to be a mechanical engineer when I want to be,” she said. “I get to be an electrical engineer when I want to be. I get to be a firmware engineer when I want to be.” The failures she chases can be immense or microscopic. A rack-scale issue might involve high-speed signaling, thermal margins or power integrity. Another might come down to a screw tightened too far or the level of dust in a customer facility. “The solution can be elusive,” Fiza said. “We have to follow the clues, ignore the red herrings and know where to look.” When a log shows how something failed, Fiza’s job is to discover why. Validation engineers reproduce the issue, vary the conditions, investigate firmware, remove mechanical variables, probe signals, study scope shots and narrow the possible causes. A single board may contain tens of thousands of components; a rack may approach half a million. Those parts must not merely coexist. They must behave as one system under stress, at scale, in the complex realities of production and deployment across diverse AI factory configurations. “I wish people understood how complex the hardware is that AI needs to run on,” Fiza said. For Fiza, the pressure of the work is inseparable from the pleasure of it. Bring-up, she said, is “like the Avengers assembling”: architects, designers, software engineers, firmware engineers, validation engineers, all in the room, racing toward a working system. “One thing I know when I come to work is I’m never alone,” she said. To be a validation engineer is to practice a disciplined kind of suspicion: believe a system can work, then try to conceive of every way it might not. The job requires the doggedness of a great detective, as well as the diagnostic abilities of a general practitioner and the temperament of someone who meets catastrophic failure in the way others might a crossword. Each project brings a new puzzle, a new failure mode and, in turn, a chance to make the next system better. “With the products we have in the pipeline, I’m so excited,” Fiza said. “They’re going to change the world.”

items.titleZh: 萨基娜·菲扎助力英伟达硬件大规模成功
items.descriptionZh:
这篇报道以NVIDIA验证工程师Sakeena Fiza为切入点，介绍了AI数据中心系统在量产和交付客户之前所经历的验证工作。Fiza在加州大学欧文分校学习计算机科学与工程，成长于迪拜，早年通过Logo语言接触编程，并在高中机器人营中参与火星车项目、大学期间研究无人机，最终被数据中心系统的“整机”问题吸引，加入NVIDIA。她的工作地点位于圣克拉拉办公室的数据中心系统工程实验室。

她将验证工作比作侦探破案：拿到一套系统时，第一反应不是它如何工作，而是“它可能会怎么坏？”一旦系统出现问题，就把它当作谜题来追查。验证工程发生在产品对外公开之前：新系统首次上电后，组件逐个启动，板卡完成集成，固件和软件团队协同介入，工程师等待系统出现“生命迹象”。她最难忘的经历之一，是在系统层面首次看到NVIDIA Rubin GPU工作。当时日志只显示“NVIDIA Corporation Device”，全场欢呼，因为这是全球首次Rubin GPU在系统级完成枚举。此后，系统还必须从托盘到机架、集群、产线，再到客户的AI工厂，逐级变得可靠。

Fiza把验证团队称为产品的“第一批客户”：在量产开始前，在多种真实条件下把硬件逼到极限，目标是在客户发现问题之前先发现并解决问题。原文没有给出具体性能跑分或竞品对比数据，但提供了复杂度指标：一块板可能包含数万个组件，一个机架可能接近50万个组件。这些部件不能只是简单共存，而必须在压力、规模和多样化AI工厂部署条件下，作为一个完整系统协同工作。

验证工作横跨固件、硬件、软件、机械设计、热管理、制造和客户体验。故障可能来自机架级高速信号、热余量或电源完整性，也可能只是螺丝拧得过紧，或客户设施中的灰尘水平。验证工程师需要复现问题、改变条件、排查固件、排除机械变量、探测信号、分析示波器截图，并逐步缩小可能原因。Fiza说，解决方案可能难以捉摸，必须跟随线索、忽略误导，并知道该往哪里看。

她形容系统点亮和调试过程像“复仇者联盟集结”：架构师、设计人员、软件工程师、固件工程师和验证工程师同处一室，共同冲刺到系统可用。验证工程师需要侦探般的执着、全科医生般的诊断能力，以及把灾难性故障当作填字游戏来面对的心态。每个项目都会带来新谜题、新失效模式，以及让下一代系统变得更好的机会。Fiza表示，她对公司在研产品非常兴奋，并认为这些产品将改变世界。

items.title: China's ByteDance gained access to over 2,000 Nvidia B200 chips through Norway data center
items.description: UK-based Nscale signed a deal with Spring (SG) Pte Ltd, which is a subsidiary of Chinese tech giant ByteDance. The company did not make any direct mention of the TikTok parent in its filings for a U.S. IPO, while a supporting document only labeled Spring as a significant customer.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter UK-based “neocloud” Nscale built its business on a major deal with a ByteDance subsidiary named Spring, which accounted for $24 million of its $33 million annual revenue in 2025. This contract allowed Spring to access 2,304 Nvidia B200 chips at Nscale’s Glomfjord, Norway, data center. Even though the Financial Times reports that this was legal and exploited loopholes in the U.S.’s ongoing export controls against China, it still exposes the company to regulatory and reputational risk, especially as Washington continues to restrict Chinese access to its most advanced AI accelerators.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleThis information only came to light after Nscale released its S-1 documents as it filed for an initial public offering in the U.S. There was also no direct mention of the TikTok owner or its subsidiary anywhere in its S-1 filing; instead, it was noted in a supporting document, a $105 million loan agreement with Macquarie, that Spring (SG) Pte Ltd, a Singaporean ByteDance subsidiary, was a significant customer. This credit, alongside a $35 million in equity, helped fund the purchase of advanced Nvidia AI GPUs, which also caught the attention of the chipmaker.A month after Nscale drew the first tranche of the loan, it closed a deal with Microsoft and Nvidia, with Jensen Huang committing to invest more than $660 million into the company. This funding is part of an agreement between Nscale and Nvidia, under which the latter promised to buy large volumes of AI chips in the future. Nvidia has since increased its commitments to over $2 billion, plus an additional $860 million guarantee on Nscale’s lease at a Texas facility. Nscale has since been able to secure larger deals with other AI hyperscalers, such as a $44 billion deal with Microsoft and another $45 billion contract with Anthropic. The company said that this would make its Spring contract fall to below 20% of its overall revenue, and it is expected to shrink further as Nscale secures other Western clients.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Because of Spring’s link to ByteDance, Macquarie compelled Nscale to monitor how the Chinese subsidiary used the AI chips and report “compute anomalies or suspicious configurations” that might be in violation of the U.S.’s export controls. Nscale also had a third party conduct due diligence on both the TikTok parent and the Singapore-based subsidiary to ensure that the deal complied with the law.Chinese companies have been taking advantage of these loopholes in the U.S.’s export controls to gain access to advanced AI chips. While they cannot import the most advanced Nvidia AI GPUs, like Blackwell and Vera Rubin, into China, they could still rent these AI chips from companies based abroad or by using subsidiaries founded outside of China to purchase them directly. However, the U.S. has recently closed the latter loophole, with the Trump administration working to close the former, too. It’s unclear if these moves would affect the Spring-Nscale deal, but the recent delays on gigawatt-scale data center projects in the U.S. mean that Nscale could potentially get more clients as AI hyperscalers race to secure compute from smaller facilities. items.titleZh: 中国字节跳动通过挪威数据中心获得逾2000块英伟达B200芯片
items.descriptionZh:
英国新型云服务商 Nscale 因一份与字节跳动子公司 Spring 的合同而受到关注。Nscale 在申请美国 IPO 时发布的 S-1 文件及相关支持文件披露，Spring (SG) Pte Ltd 是其重要客户。2025 年 Nscale 年收入为 3300 万美元，其中 Spring 贡献 2400 万美元，约占七成。该合同允许 Spring 使用 Nscale 位于挪威 Glomfjord 数据中心的 2304 块英伟达 B200 AI GPU。英国《金融时报》称，这项安排虽然合法，但利用了美国对华出口管制中的漏洞。由于华盛顿持续限制中国获取最先进 AI 加速器，这类交易仍使 Nscale 面临监管与声誉风险。

背景上，中国公司无法直接进口英伟达最先进 AI GPU，例如 Blackwell 和 Vera Rubin，但可以通过两种方式绕开：一是从海外公司租用算力，二是利用设在境外的子公司直接购买。Spring 作为字节跳动的新加坡子公司，签约租用挪威数据中心的算力，芯片物理上不进入中国，因此避开了直接出口限制。B200 属于英伟达 Blackwell 代际的数据中心 AI 加速器，面向大模型训练和推理，是当时受管制的高端芯片之一。该交易细节最初并未出现在 S-1 正文中，而是出现在与麦格理签订的 1.05 亿美元贷款协议支持文件里。该贷款加上 3500 万美元股权，帮助 Nscale 购买先进英伟达 AI GPU，并引起英伟达注意。麦格理要求 Nscale 监控 Spring 如何使用这些 AI 芯片，并报告可能违反美国出口管制的“计算异常或可疑配置”。Nscale 还委托第三方对字节跳动及 Spring 进行尽职调查，以确保交易合法。

此后，Nscale 的资本和客户结构发生剧变。在提取首笔贷款一个月后，Nscale 与微软和英伟达达成交易，黄仁勋承诺向 Nscale 投资超过 6.6 亿美元。作为 Nscale 与英伟达协议的一部分，英伟达承诺未来购买大量 AI 芯片，后来将承诺额提高至超过 20 亿美元，并额外为 Nscale 在得州设施的租赁提供 8.6 亿美元担保。Nscale 还获得了与微软的 440 亿美元协议、与 Anthropic 的 450 亿美元合同。公司称，这些大单将使 Spring 合同占其总收入比例降至 20% 以下，并随着西方客户增加而继续缩小。

从技术影响看，这一事件说明出口管制可能被“境外算力租赁”模式绕过：芯片留在境外数据中心，中国背景企业通过海外子公司租用云端 AI 算力，仍可训练和推理大模型。其关键并非芯片技术本身，而是利用云服务跨境交付与出口管制主要针对硬件出口之间的边界。美国已关闭中国公司利用海外子公司直接购买芯片的漏洞，特朗普政府也在推动限制境外云算力服务。这些措施是否会影响 Spring-Nscale 交易尚不清楚。但美国吉瓦级数据中心项目近期出现延迟，AI 超大规模企业争抢较小设施的算力，Nscale 等 neocloud 可能因此获得更多西方客户，进一步降低对中国收入的依赖。另据页面相关报道，首批英伟达 H200 已在个案进口许可下运抵中国，字节跳动和腾讯提货，美国也允许中兴购买 H200，显示出口管制与执行仍在动态变化。

items.title: Alibaba unveils Zhenwu V900 AI accelerator, claims it's 'the most powerful AI chip in China'
items.description: Alibaba’s T-Head Zhenwu V900 claims three times the M890’s performance with 216GB of memory as Alibaba targets 10T-parameter Qwen
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Alibaba unveiled its powerful new Zhenwu V900 chip and ambitious Qwen model plans at the Apsara Conference 2026, the AP reports. Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu calls the Zhenwu 900 the most powerful AI chip in China, with three times the performance of the previous-generation M890. The chip is meant to support the training of future Qwen models in the 5 to 10 trillion parameter range, an increase over both the 2.4 trillion Qwen3.8-Max and Moonshot’s Kimi K3 and its 2.8 trillion parameter basis. The announcement follows Huawei’s new chip launch last week.Alibaba describes the Zhenwu V900 as an AI training and inference processor with 216 GB of GPU memory and 1,200 GB/s of inter-chip bandwidth. Aside from performance being multiples of the last generation, the chip can scale out to a supernode cluster “comprising up to 500,000 cards.” The AI accelerator is due for mass production and commercial release in the first quarter of 2027, Alibaba says.The company’s May roadmap placed the V900 in the third quarter of 2027, so the timeline has moved up. As of May, Alibaba chip arm T-Head had shipped more than 560,000 Zhenwu chips to over 400 external customers, a count Alibaba now puts above 650, with a Zhenwu refresh expected annually.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The technical specifications do not include FLOPS, a process node, foundry, power figures, or memory bandwidth claims. The prior M890 had 144GB of memory with 800GB/s of inter-chip bandwidth. The M890 could work in a supernode of 128 chips, while T-Head says more than 1,000 V900 chips can work as a single system.For comparison, Huawei’s Ascend 960PR, due in the third quarter of 2027, is slated for 192GB of memory capacity, 2.4TB/s of memory bandwidth, and a 2.2TB/s scale-up interconnect. Alibaba’s most-powerful and three-times claims currently rest on no absolute figure for compute, but maximum achievable FLOPS are often far below calculated figures to begin with, so delivered performance will be the ultimate judge. You may like Z.ai powers up a 1-gigawatt AI data center built entirely on Chinese chips, report claims Huawei details AI accelerator roadmap, pulls in next-generation Ascend NPUs by several quarters China's 2.8 trillion-parameter Kimi K3 beats Claude Fable 5 in Frontend Code Arena Alibaba Cloud’s greater goal is to reach a data center capacity of “more than 20 gigawatts” by 2032, the company said. However, global shortages in the AI supply chain “are currently limiting the speed at which we can scale our compute infrastructure,” Wu said. Alibaba also anticipates significant growth in its own annual AI chip shipments. Domestic demand remains high as Huawei had to shelve its global Ascend rollout. The report compared these goals to SpaceX, which has around 1.4GW of AI compute with a target of more than 10GW in 2027.On the model side, Qwen 4 is “currently in training,” Alibaba said, and the Qwen 4.5 and 5 families will scale up further on the roadmap. As far as the achievements of its current models go, the company claims that Qwen3.8-Max ran “33 iterative cycles” over a month of automated runs to produce an Artificial Analysis score gain from 40 to 45. Meanwhile, a separate chip-design experiment with more than 10,000 EDA tool calls over more than 60 hours of test time showed an area cut of 42% without performance loss.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsThe announcements come ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping’s summit with President Donald Trump in Washington on Thursday. AI remains a top subject on the agenda, following U.S.-proposed AI mechanisms. The AI talks in New York did not have export controls for chips or tools on the agenda.As it stands, Alibaba’s V900 is months from commercial release and the 5-to-10-trillion-parameter model it promises remains untrained. Capacity targets remain six years out. The announcement is nevertheless timely as the two largest national AI powers come together to discuss and define AI security. items.titleZh: 阿里巴巴发布真武V900 AI加速器，号称“中国最强AI芯片”
items.descriptionZh:
据美联社报道，在2026年云栖大会上，阿里巴巴发布了新一代AI芯片真武V900（Zhenwu 900），并公布了野心勃勃的通义千问（Qwen）模型计划。阿里巴巴CEO吴泳铭称，真武900是中国目前最强的AI芯片，性能达到上一代M890的三倍。该芯片旨在支持未来5万亿至10万亿参数级别的Qwen模型训练，这一规模超过Qwen3.8-Max的2.4万亿参数，也超过月之暗面Kimi K3的2.8万亿参数基础。此次发布距离华为上周推出新芯片仅过去一周，凸显中国AI芯片竞争正在加速。

真武V900被阿里描述为面向AI训练和推理的处理器，配备216GB GPU显存和1200GB/s片间带宽。其核心创新之一在于扩展能力：除了性能较上代成倍提升，还可向外扩展至由最多50万张卡组成的超级节点集群。阿里表示，该AI加速器将于2027年第一季度量产并商用发布。这比公司5月路线图中原定的2027年第三季度有所提前。截至今年5月，阿里芯片部门平头哥已向400多家外部客户出货超过56万颗真武芯片；阿里现在称这一数字已超过65万颗，并预计真武系列每年都会更新。

不过，官方技术规格并未披露浮点运算能力（FLOPS）、工艺节点、代工厂、功耗数据或内存带宽。作为对比，上一代M890拥有144GB内存和800GB/s片间带宽，可组成128颗芯片的超级节点；而平头哥称，1000多颗V900可作为单一系统协同工作。与华为相比，计划于2027年第三季度推出的昇腾960PR预计具备192GB内存容量、2.4TB/s内存带宽和2.2TB/s纵向扩展互连。阿里“最强”和“三倍性能”的说法目前没有绝对算力数字支撑；而最大可达FLOPS通常一开始就远低于理论计算值，因此实际交付性能才是最终评判标准。

在基础设施层面，阿里云更大的目标是到2032年实现“超过20吉瓦”的数据中心容量。但吴泳铭表示，全球AI供应链短缺“目前限制了我们扩展计算基础设施的速度”。阿里还预计自身年度AI芯片出货量将显著增长。由于华为不得不搁置昇腾的全球推广，中国国内需求仍然很高。报告将阿里的目标与SpaceX对比：后者目前拥有约1.4吉瓦AI算力，目标是在2027年超过10吉瓦。

模型方面，阿里表示Qwen 4“目前正在训练中”，Qwen 4.5和Qwen 5系列将在路线图中进一步扩展。就当前模型成果而言，阿里称Qwen3.8-Max在一个月的自动化运行中执行了“33次迭代循环”，使Artificial Analysis得分从40提升至45。与此同时，另一项芯片设计实验在超过60小时测试时间内调用超过10000次EDA工具，结果显示面积减少42%且没有性能损失。

这些公告发布在中国国家主席习近平与美国总统特朗普周四在华盛顿举行峰会之前。AI仍是峰会议程上的首要议题之一，此前美国提出了相关AI机制。纽约的AI会谈并未将芯片或工具出口管制列入议程。总体来看，阿里V900距离商用发布还有数月，其承诺支持的5万亿至10万亿参数模型也尚未训练，20吉瓦容量目标更是六年后的事情。但此次发布时机仍然敏感而及时，因为全球两个最大的AI国家力量正走到一起，讨论并定义AI安全。

Combo deals certainly help to bring this outlandish pricing down to something reasonable for the time being. This gray Corsair Vengeance DDR5-6000 kit is now $439 with promo code SSF73844 and is the cheapest standalone kit we could find right now matching our white 32GB V-Color Manta XSky kit we found earlier this week for less, but that’s now the same price. Check out this deal at Newegg Deals like this, and the combos when active, are by far the best way to buy new RAM in the ongoing RAMpocalypse. Sadly, the days when you can get 64GB of DDR5-6400 RAM for around $225 (what I paid for a G.Skill Trident Z Royale kit in April 2025) are over, and you’re left with what we have now…the best prices in an extremely expensive market.As for this specific Corsair Vengeance kit, it’s a great option for any build, performance-wise. The DDR5-6000 speed sits squarely in AMD’s sweet spot for price-to-performance and is much faster than older DDR4 modules. Sadly, we didn’t review this specific kit, but below are performance numbers from a similar DDR5-6000 CL38 kit from Team Group (Vulcan CL38 kit) that show how well it performs in our CPU test suite.Save $85Corsair 32GB Vengeance DDR5-6000 CL38: was $524.99 now $439.99 at NeweggSave big on this 32GB (2x16GB) Corsair Vengeance DDR5-6000 CL38 kit in gray and get your new system, or upgraded RAM moving for less.View Deal (Image credit: Future)The Corsair Vengeance kit comes in gray without RGB lighting and includes two DDR5-6000 modules with CL38-48-48-96 timings at 1.35V. Though the timings are a bit higher than we’d like to see, they'll work well for any use case, from gaming to workstation productivity, and you’ll get the most out of your system at these speeds, especially on the AM5 platform. If you were considering this kit for an Intel system, it will also work well, but is a bit on the slower side for the platform.While $439 for 32GB of Corsair Vengeance DDR5-6000 RAM (read: any RAM) makes most of us shudder in disappointment these days, considering what RAM prices were in early 2025, it is one of the best deals available for 32GB DDR5-6000 in gray/black. If you’re in the market to start a DDR5-based build or upgrade what you have and need it soon, I wouldn’t pass up this Newegg deal.

items.titleZh: This 32GB Corsair Vengeance DDR5-6000 memory is the cheapest kit available
items.descriptionZh:
当前DRAM市场仍处于“内存末日”（RAMpocalypse）状态，价格高企且短期内难以回落。在此背景下，组合优惠和单品促销成为降低装机成本的主要途径。本文介绍了一款灰色Corsair Vengeance DDR5-6000 32GB（2×16GB）内存套件，使用优惠码SSF73844后售价439美元，原价524.99美元，节省85美元。这是目前能找到的最便宜独立32GB DDR5-6000套件之一，与本周早些时候发现的白色32GB V-Color Manta XSky套件价格相同（后者此前更便宜）。文章指出，2025年4月曾能以约225美元买到64GB DDR5-6400内存（如G.Skill Trident Z Royale），那样的时代已经结束。

技术参数方面，该Corsair Vengeance套件为灰色无RGB设计，包含两条DDR5-6000模块，时序CL38-48-48-96，电压1.35V。虽然时序略高于理想值，但足以满足从游戏到工作站生产力的各类需求。DDR5-6000速度正好处于AMD AM5平台性价比甜点，显著快于老款DDR4模块。在Intel平台上也能正常工作，但相对该平台而言速度稍慢。文章未评测该具体套件，但引用了类似Team Group DDR5-6000 CL38套件（Vulcan CL38）在CPU测试套件中的性能数据，表明其性能表现良好。

应用场景与影响：这款内存适合新建DDR5系统或升级现有平台，尤其推荐给需要尽快购入的用户。尽管439美元对32GB DDR5而言仍令大多数人感到失望，但考虑到2025年初的内存价格，它已是灰色/黑色32GB DDR5-6000中最佳交易之一。对于正在考虑DDR5装机或升级且时间紧迫的用户，不应错过Newegg的这次促销。

items.title: China launches 'Supercomputing-1' AI satellite as orbital data centers gather momentum
items.description: But it's a far cry from an orbital data center.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter China has launched nine satellites — including its first integrated “rocket and satellite” AI computing project — as part of its push to put AI computing in orbit. According to a Digitimes report, the Kinetica 1 Y18 rocket, operated by Chinese commercial launch provider CAS Space, lifted off on September 20, carrying the nine satellites to their planned orbits.The payload of greatest interest is the “Supercomputing-1” satellite, developed by Chinese AI computing infrastructure company S-AIDC. Also known as the S-AIDC-1, the satellite is designed to capture and process Earth-observation data in orbit instead of sending data back to terrestrial data centers. Keeping the processing local is meant to cut cross-regional data processing times from hours to minutes. The satellite features both a high-res optical payload and the image-processing AI computer.According to Digitimes, the launch highlights China's efforts to develop orbital computing as part of a “broader integrated computing network.” In early June, the Chinese government approved the Space Computing Industry Innovation Center, which aims to bring together rocket and satellite manufacturers, semiconductor fabs, and AI tech companies to build a space computing network. A couple of factors are driving this spike in the development of off-planet computing, foremost among them being the AI boom.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The demand for artificial intelligence has spurred the construction of numerous data centers to house AI accelerators. These data centers, some of which can house hundreds of thousands of accelerators, consume unprecedented amounts of electricity, placing significant strain on the grid. This, along with land use, water consumption for cooling, and noise, has fueled growing anti-data sentiment, with local residents blocking $68 billion worth of new data center projects in Q2 2026.Despite numerous economic and practical challenges, space might offer an alternative with unlimited area, access to solar power, constant cold conditions, and a dead-quiet vacuum. These advantages have made orbital computing a serious topic of discussion. SpaceX is leading the charge with the AI1 satellite, a proposed orbital data center that will deliver 150 kW of peak compute power. The company aims to achieve 1 GW per year of space AI compute by 2027 and has begun constructing the 11-million-square-foot Gigasat facility that would manufacture the 6,000 satellites required to meet this goal. You may like Intel's proposed two-tier satellite network puts the brains of satellite constellations in higher orbit Z.ai powers up a 1-gigawatt AI data center built entirely on Chinese chips, report claims China shifting massive AI data center complexes to rural provinces to tap surplus energy Beyond the large-scale serving of AI models, putting edge compute capacity in space is already useful for a range of applications. Earth-observation satellites can process images onboard to identify wildfires, storms, floods, ships, or other objects of interest, sending only the useful results back to Earth instead of dumping enormous amounts of raw data to ground stations. The same approach can speed up weather monitoring, disaster response, communications, and even the management of satellite constellations, where spacecraft could make more decisions independently rather than waiting for instructions from Earth.The launch of a single satellite with edge AI capabilities on board is a far cry from an entire orbital data center, but China's approach could prove to be a more practical and immediate application for advanced computing capabilities in orbit.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, oradd us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.

items.titleZh: 中国发射“超算一号”AI卫星，轨道数据中心发展势头正劲
items.descriptionZh:
中国近期用一枚商业火箭将九颗卫星送入预定轨道，其中包含其首个“火箭与卫星”一体化AI计算项目，标志着中国推动AI算力上轨迈出实质性一步。据Digitimes报道，中国商业发射商中科宇航（CAS Space）运营的Kinetica 1 Y18火箭于9月20日点火升空，把九颗卫星送入目标轨道。最受关注的载荷是由中国AI计算基础设施公司S-AIDC研发的“Supercomputing-1”卫星，也称S-AIDC-1。该卫星的设计目标是在轨直接捕获并处理地球观测数据，而不是把海量原始数据传回地面数据中心后再处理。通过把处理环节留在太空，跨区域数据处理时间可从数小时缩短到数分钟。卫星同时搭载高分辨率光学载荷和用于图像处理的AI计算机，本质上是一颗具备星载边缘AI能力的遥感卫星。

这一发射凸显中国正在把轨道计算纳入“更广泛的集成计算网络”。此前在6月初，中国政府批准设立空间计算产业创新中心，计划把火箭和卫星制造商、半导体晶圆厂以及AI技术公司联合起来，共同建设空间计算网络。推动这一趋势的关键因素首先是AI热潮。AI需求刺激大量数据中心建设，用于容纳AI加速器，其中一些数据中心可部署数十万个加速器，耗电量空前，给电网带来巨大压力。与此同时，土地占用、冷却用水和噪音等问题也引发日益强烈的反数据中心情绪；原文称，当地居民在2026年第二季度阻止了价值680亿美元的新数据中心项目。相比之下，太空可能提供一种替代方案：面积几乎不受限制、可直接利用太阳能、环境持续低温，并且真空环境极为安静。这些优势使轨道计算成为严肃讨论方向。

在竞争层面，SpaceX目前走在前列。其提出的AI1卫星是一个轨道数据中心方案，可提供150千瓦峰值计算功率。SpaceX计划到2027年实现每年1吉瓦的太空AI算力，并已开始建设占地1100万平方英尺的Gigasat设施，用于制造实现该目标所需的6000颗卫星。与中国此次发射的单颗边缘AI卫星相比，SpaceX的规划规模更大，更接近“整座轨道数据中心”的构想。

但把边缘算力部署到太空，本身已经有一系列现实用途。地球观测卫星可以在轨处理图像，识别野火、风暴、洪水和船只等目标，只把有用结果传回地球，而不是向地面站倾倒海量原始数据。类似方法还可加速天气监测、灾害响应、通信，甚至卫星星座管理，使航天器能够更独立地做出决策，而不必等待地球指令。总体来看，发射一颗具备边缘AI能力的卫星距离完整的轨道数据中心仍很遥远，但中国的路径可能是一种更务实、更即时的先进计算在轨应用方式。

items.title: At AI Day Singapore, NVIDIA and Partners Showcase AI Advancements Across Southeast Asia
items.description: NVIDIA AI Day Singapore, which takes place Sept. 22-23 at the Raffles City Convention Centre, is offering attendees opportunities to explore the hands-on training, expert-led sessions and advanced tools to accelerate their work in AI and high-performance computing. At the event, NVIDIA and its partners are showcasing breakthrough AI advancements across the Southeast Asia region […]
items.content: NVIDIA AI Day Singapore, which takes place Sept. 22-23 at the Raffles City Convention Centre, is offering attendees opportunities to explore the hands-on training, expert-led sessions and advanced tools to accelerate their work in AI and high-performance computing. At the event, NVIDIA and its partners are showcasing breakthrough AI advancements across the Southeast Asia region at large. Read more about these announcements below. NVIDIA Accelerates Public Sector AI from Pilot to Production in Southeast Asia 🔗 AI is becoming a matter of national strategy, with governments looking to move from pilots to production and deliver impact at scale, while building trusted AI capabilities that reflect local languages, cultures, priorities and economic needs. NVIDIA is working to enable all nations to be AI nations — providing the technology, infrastructure, ecosystem and expertise needed to make this possible. To accelerate this transition across Southeast Asia, NVIDIA is helping nations move AI from experimentation to production-scale deployment through open models, developer tools and a broad partner ecosystem. Together, NVIDIA and its partners are focusing on four key areas: Enhancing government operations and service delivery. Developing accessible AI-powered citizen services, and empowering local businesses. Strengthening critical infrastructure and public safety. Supporting startups, developers and researchers to strengthen national AI capabilities and innovation in each country. Singapore’s HTX (Home Team Science and Technology Agency) is embarking on research using the NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super and Nemotron 3 Nano Omni models to advance AI for public safety. Nemotron Super has the potential to support the agency’s complex reasoning and agentic workflows, while Omni’s unified vision, audio and language capabilities could help HTX develop multimodal applications grounded in real-world operational data. Together, the models could strengthen HTX’s ability to deploy secure, locally controlled AI across Singapore’s Home Team. NCS is advancing agentic AI adoption across enterprises and the public sector, using Nemotron models and the NVIDIA Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS), while advancing physical AI for practical humanoid robotics applications, to address security, responsiveness and data governance requirements. ST Engineering is using NVIDIA NeMo tools and NVIDIA cuOpt software to develop its AI Studio platform and deploy agentic AI solutions across its businesses such as Marine MRO. Beyond Singapore, similar work is already underway across the region. Malaysia’s YTL AI Labs is fine-tuning Nemotron models for enterprise and citizen services, while Viettel AI is doing the same for Vietnamese-language applications. In Thailand, the Big Data Institute and iApp Technology, as members of the ThaiLLM Collaboration, are exploring Nemotron as a foundation model. With an initial focus on legal applications, iApp Technology is adapting Nemotron 3 Nano by fine-tuning OpenThai 2.0 Legal with Thai-language legal data using the NVIDIA NeMo framework. The model is released as open source for the Thai developer community and serves as the engine for Thanoy, the company’s legal-assistant chatbot, which already serves approximately 43,000 users. In Brunei, Antrique built an AI innovation platform to help boost productivity across the nation’s food sector. Across the region, NVIDIA Cosmos open world models and the NVIDIA VSS Blueprint are advancing smart city solution development. Malaysia’s ITMAX uses Cosmos with VSS to improve city traffic operations, while Thailand’s AS-TECH applies the same stack to improve passenger flow in airports. Learn more about NVIDIA Nemotron and Cosmos models and read about NVIDIA’s participation in the Open Secure AI Alliance. Southeast Asia Technology Leaders Build With NVIDIA Nemotron Open Models for Region-Specialized AI 🔗 Leading enterprises, technology providers and research organizations across Southeast Asia are building region-specialized AI models and applications with NVIDIA Nemotron open models, datasets and libraries — accelerating the development of AI tailored to the region’s languages, industries and communities. NVIDIA Nemotron provides a foundation for regional AI ecosystems, letting organizations customize, control and own models that address their specific requirements. Nemotron also offers persona datasets that provide locally relevant synthetic data reflecting the region’s populations, languages and workforces. Across the region, partners are building applications spanning public services, services and healthcare. NVIDIA Nemotron Adoption Expands in Singapore Enterprises in Singapore are adopting NVIDIA Nemotron for various use cases. AI Singapore is expanding its SEA-LION model family to include the NVIDIA Nemotron open models and NVIDIA NeMo tools. SEA-LION is an open model family designed for Southeast Asian languages and cultures. Hummingbird Bioscience, together with LynxKite, is building an explainable Toxicity Knowledge Graph powered by Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and NeMo Retriever with in silico simulations. The collaboration aims to integrate complex public and proprietary data across diverse third-party file formats, creating a comprehensive, unified foundation for robust analysis and reasoning that helps de-risk and accelerate drug discovery and development. Across Asia Pacific, NVIDIA Nemotron Enables Region-Specific AI Bitdeer AI co-hosted the Open Models AI Codefest with NVIDIA, providing the GPU cloud infrastructure that enabled developers across the region to use NVIDIA Nemotron open models, datasets and training recipes to accelerate localized applications across critical sectors, including healthcare. In Vietnam, Viettel AI has been extensively fine-tuning Nemotron 3 Super for the Vietnamese language and agentic applications. The model achieved the highest ranking on both the VMLU benchmark and the company’s in-house product benchmark, and it’s set to be adopted in Legal AI — an agent harness that will serve both internal Viettel Group employees and external customers. Also in Vietnam, FPT Smart Cloud codeveloped Nemotron-Personas-Vietnam, an open dataset grounded in Vietnamese demographic and cultural data, and is enabling local developers to post-train and evaluate localized AI models. Get started building with NVIDIA Nemotron using skills and playbooks that help partners customize Nemotron open models for their languages and domains. Stay up to date on agentic AI, NVIDIA Nemotron and more by subscribing to NVIDIA news, joining the community and following NVIDIA AI on LinkedIn, Instagram, X and Facebook. Explore self-paced video tutorials and livestreams. Sea the First in ASEAN Region to Adopt NVIDIA Vera Rubin, Scaling AI to Better Serve Communities Across Southeast Asia 🔗 Sea Limited, a global technology company founded in Singapore, is the first enterprise in the ASEAN region to adopt the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform, further strengthening the company’s AI capabilities to better serve and create meaningful economic opportunities for millions of consumers and small businesses across Southeast Asia. Serving hundreds of millions of users through its Garena, Monee and Shopee platforms, Sea has already deployed AI across its businesses to make its services more useful and accessible. Now, with NVIDIA Vera Rubin, Sea will build on these efforts, developing and deploying AI models and intelligent agents at greater scale to serve the evolving needs of its communities. On Shopee, AI is already helping sellers reduce the time and effort required to create informative product listings, improve product discovery and deepen customer engagement, while enabling better-informed business decisions. These capabilities enable small- and medium-sized enterprises in Southeast Asia, many of which operate with limited resources, to scale their businesses using enterprise-grade AI technologies previously accessible only to large corporations. Across Monee, the digital financial services division of Sea, AI is being applied in areas such as fraud detection and credit risk assessment, supporting Monee’s ability to deliver simple, accessible and inclusive digital financial services. For small businesses and consumers underserved by traditional financial services, these capabilities can expansively broaden access to financial tools. At Garena, Sea’s digital entertainment and video game arm, AI is used to enhance gaming experiences supporting the company’s efforts to create engaging, inclusive and safe online spaces that bring players together. NVIDIA Vera Rubin will provide the advanced computing infrastructure to build on this foundation — enabling Sea to accelerate innovation, scale AI applications more broadly and deepen its impact for the communities it serves. Learn more about NVIDIA Vera Rubin.

NVIDIA AI Day Singapore 于9月22日至23日在新加坡莱佛士城会议中心举行。此次大会的核心背景是，AI 正在成为国家战略：东南亚各国政府希望把 AI 从零散试点推向生产级部署，并建立反映本地语言、文化、优先事项和经济需求的可信 AI 能力。NVIDIA 提出的目标是“让所有国家都能成为 AI 国家”，通过技术、基础设施、生态和专业知识帮助各国完成这一转型。大会期间，NVIDIA 及其合作伙伴集中展示了东南亚地区在公共部门 AI、区域专用开放模型、企业智能体、多模态应用以及新一代 AI 计算平台方面的进展。

在公共部门 AI 方面，NVIDIA 正与合作伙伴推动东南亚从实验走向规模化生产，重点覆盖四个方向：提升政府运营和服务交付；开发可访问的 AI 公民服务并赋能本地企业；加强关键基础设施和公共安全；支持初创企业、开发者和研究者，强化各国 AI 能力与创新。新加坡内政团队科技局 HTX 将研究使用 NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super 和 Nemotron 3 Nano Omni 模型推进公共安全 AI。其中，Nemotron 3 Super 有望支持复杂推理和智能体工作流，Nemotron 3 Nano Omni 则统一视觉、音频和语言能力，可帮助 HTX 开发基于真实操作数据的多模态应用，并增强部署安全、本地可控 AI 的能力。NCS 使用 Nemotron 模型和 NVIDIA 视频搜索与摘要蓝图 VSS 推进企业和公共部门智能体 AI，同时探索人形机器人等物理 AI 应用，以满足安全、响应性和数据治理要求。ST Engineering 则利用 NVIDIA NeMo 工具和 cuOpt 软件开发 AI Studio 平台，并在海事维护、修理和大修等业务中部署智能体 AI。

这一趋势已扩展至整个东南亚。马来西亚 YTL AI Labs 正在微调 Nemotron 模型，用于企业和公民服务；越南 Viettel AI 面向越南语应用进行类似工作；泰国 Big Data Institute 和 iApp Technology 作为 ThaiLLM Collaboration 成员，探索将 Nemotron 作为基础模型。iApp Technology 初期聚焦法律应用，使用 NVIDIA NeMo 框架，基于 OpenThai 2.0 Legal，用泰语法律数据微调 Nemotron 3 Nano，并将模型开源给泰国开发者社区。该模型还作为其法律助手聊天机器人 Thanoy 的引擎，目前已服务约 43,000 名用户。文莱 Antrique 构建 AI 创新平台，帮助提升国家食品行业生产力。在智慧城市方面，NVIDIA Cosmos 开放世界模型和 VSS 蓝图被用于区域方案开发：马来西亚 ITMAX 用 Cosmos 与 VSS 改善城市交通运营，泰国 AS-TECH 用同一技术栈改善机场客流。

在区域专用 AI 模型方面，东南亚领先企业、技术提供商和研究机构正基于 NVIDIA Nemotron 开放模型、数据集和库构建本地化 AI。Nemotron 为区域 AI 生态提供基础，使组织能够定制、控制和拥有满足自身需求的模型。其 persona 数据集可提供反映区域人口、语言和劳动力特征的本地相关合成数据。新加坡 AI Singapore 正在扩展 SEA-LION 模型家族，纳入 NVIDIA Nemotron 开放模型和 NeMo 工具。SEA-LION 是面向东南亚语言和文化的开放模型家族。Hummingbird Bioscience 与 LynxKite 合作，使用 Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 和 NeMo Retriever，结合计算机模拟，构建可解释的毒性知识图谱。该合作旨在整合跨多种第三方文件格式的复杂公共和专有数据，形成统一分析推理基础，从而降低药物发现与开发风险并加速进程。Bitdeer AI 与 NVIDIA 共同举办 Open Models AI Codefest，提供 GPU 云基础设施，让区域开发者使用 Nemotron 开放模型、数据集和训练配方，加速医疗等关键行业的本地化应用。越南 Viettel AI 对 Nemotron 3 Super 进行大量越南语和智能体应用微调，该模型在 VMLU 基准和公司内部产品基准上均排名最高，并计划用于 Legal AI 智能体工具，服务 Viettel 集团内部员工和外部客户。越南 FPT Smart Cloud 则共同开发 Nemotron-Personas-Vietnam 开放数据集，基于越南人口和文化数据，帮助本地开发者后训练和评估本地化 AI 模型。

在企业级 AI 基础设施方面，新加坡创立的全球科技公司 Sea Limited 成为东盟地区首个采用 NVIDIA Vera Rubin 平台的企业。Sea 通过 Garena、Monee 和 Shopee 服务数亿用户，并已在各业务中部署 AI。Shopee 利用 AI 帮助卖家减少创建商品信息的时间和精力，改善产品发现和客户参与，并支持更明智的业务决策，使资源有限的东南亚中小企业也能使用过去只有大企业才能获得的企业级 AI 技术。Monee 作为 Sea 的数字金融服务部门，将 AI 用于欺诈检测和信用风险评估，帮助提供简单、可及和包容的数字金融服务，扩大传统金融服务不足的小企业和消费者获得金融工具的机会。Garena 则用 AI 增强游戏体验，打造更具参与感、包容性和安全性的在线空间。NVIDIA Vera Rubin 将提供先进计算基础设施，使 Sea 能加速创新、更广泛地扩展 AI 应用，并深化对所服务社区的影响。

从技术原理和创新点看，此次发布的核心是“开放模型 + 全栈工具 + 区域生态 + 新一代计算平台”。Nemotron 提供开放模型、数据集和库，使组织可定制、控制和拥有模型；NeMo 支持微调、后训练和评估；VSS 蓝图面向视频搜索与摘要；Cosmos 世界模型面向智慧城市和物理 AI；cuOpt 用于优化；Vera Rubin 则作为先进 AI 计算平台支撑大规模模型和智能体部署。其创新在于将主权 AI、本地语言文化适配、多模态理解、复杂推理、智能体工作流、可解释知识图谱和物理 AI 结合，推动 AI 从试点走向生产级部署。性能参数方面，原文未披露具体算力、吞吐、延迟或能效对比数据；可量化的信息包括 Viettel AI 的 Nemotron 3 Super 在 VMLU 和内部产品基准上排名最高，Thanoy 已服务约 43,000 名用户，Sea 旗下平台服务数亿用户，以及 Sea 成为东盟首个采用 Vera Rubin 的企业。整体来看，这些公告表明 NVIDIA 正通过开放模型和全栈基础设施，联合东南亚政府、企业和开发者，加速区域专用 AI、公共部门 AI 和普惠 AI 的规模化落地。

items.content: After turning a string of spectacular mathematical results into a reputational crisis, OpenAI is consulting human mathematicians to help it figure out a less disastrous path forward.On Monday, the company announced a new independent panel of mathematicians tasked with advising it and other AI companies on their interactions with mathematical research and the wider mathematics community, including how new results are presented and released. Its abrupt arrival caught many mathematicians by surprise. Researchers told The Verge the group is a good first step, but many said they were left with basic questions about what it will actually do, how much influence it will have, and whether OpenAI will actually listen to it, as well as concerns over whether such a small group of prominent researchers can represent the wider mathematical community.The nine-member group is stacked with who researchers described to The Verge as celebrities in the field, drawn from institutions including Stanford, Harvard, Oxford, and Cambridge, with multiple Fields Medals and MacArthur “genius grants” among them. It will be hosted by Princeton, New Jersey’s Institute for Advanced Study (IAS), one of the world’s most revered centers of mathematical research and the former intellectual home of figures including Albert Einstein, John von Neumann, and J. Robert Oppenheimer.“The other fundamental fact is that our overarching aim is to represent as well as we possibly can the interests of the mathematical community.”OpenAI said the group, called the Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence (AGMAI), will operate independently, with the freedom to offer advice the company has not requested, publicly comment on its impact on mathematics, and make its advice public, though it did not provide details on what this may entail. It appears that the group will be granted early access to OpenAI’s research in order to fulfill its task. Members will not be paid by OpenAI and the group can change its membership as it sees fit, OpenAI said. “Its value depends on its members being able to exercise their own judgement and challenge ours,” the company said. “The group will advise on the review and communication of emerging results: they will help OpenAI assess their significance, advise on how to coordinate their dissemination, and advise on academic and professional standards of mathematical research. It will also advise on how our tools can support mathematical research and learning.”RelatedOpenAI just wants to winOpenAI’s sly mathematical breakthrough sends a chill through academiaThe AI takeover of mathematics has begunFor all the emphasis on independence, it remains unclear how much influence the group will actually have or why it was formed in the first place. Simon Machado, a researcher at ETH Zurich in Switzerland, said the whole thing seemed “shrouded in mystery” and he questioned how the nine members were selected. The group’s bare-bones website says it “came together after OpenAI approached some of its members about establishing an external advisory board,” but that, following discussions with the company, the mathematicians decided to launch an independent group instead and invite others to join. It’s not clear which members were initially approached by OpenAI or how the remaining members were selected.In a blog post published Tuesday, advisory group member Martin Hairer elaborated on the group’s origins and the thinking behind it, responding to what he called a “torrent of misinformation” surrounding its formation. “It is obvious that AI has already had a profound impact on mathematical research and raises numerous questions of correct attribution of ideas, priority, human understanding of ideas, etc.,” he wrote, adding that there is no sense in the community “taking a hard ‘ostrich’ approach of simply ignoring the AI labs and refusing to talk to them on principle.”While acknowledging that the group was formed in response to an approach from OpenAI, Hairer stressed that not all of its members had been contacted by the company and that the resulting organization is “genuinely independent of OpenAI and any other of the so-called ‘frontier’ AI labs.” Beyond “obvious confidentiality requirements,” he said members have not signed any restrictive agreements governing what they can say publicly, adding that they receive no financial compensation and are relying on the IAS for technical support.“The other fundamental fact is that our overarching aim is to represent as well as we possibly can the interests of the mathematical community,” wrote Hairer, a professor of mathematics at Imperial College London and the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne (EPFL). While noting that the group is hardly a representative sample of the community, he said he is “absolutely certain that all nine of us take this extremely seriously and are acting in good faith.”However the members were selected, the group currently comprises an elite cadre of academic mathematicians. The small size raises further questions about whether the group has the breadth of expertise required to evaluate everything coming its way, given the highly specialized skills and knowledge required to operate at the frontiers of mathematics.Francesco Fournier-Facio, an incoming mathematics professor at Heriot-Watt University in Scotland, described himself as pretty “ambivalent” about the panel, saying that greater engagement with mathematicians “can only make things better.” But he questioned whether this group fully reflects the community whose work and livelihoods are being upended by OpenAI’s quest to rack up mathematical trophies. “It feels like an ivory tower,” he told The Verge.Machado similarly questioned whether the group’s members fully understand, or can speak to, the concerns of the broader mathematical community when it comes to AI. “They’re amazing mathematicians, but I don’t know if they are the people I want to represent me in more political questions,” he said. For mathematicians in their and similarly elite positions, Machado said, “I think that the reality they are facing is very different from the reality that most mathematicians are facing right now.”Whether the group can earn mathematicians’ trust will ultimately determine how effective it will be at containing the fallout from OpenAI’s recent parade of missteps in announcing results and, more importantly, soften the blow for whatever the company is planning to announce next. In his blog, Hairer said members would “be very naïve to believe that the AI labs won’t try to spin whatever we say in a way that suits their PR machine, which dwarfs anything we could possibly come up with.”Nevertheless, Hairer argued it would be hypocritical not to engage now that OpenAI appears to be making an effort, particularly after so many criticized the company’s conduct and poor communications. The group has yet to settle on the advice it intends to provide, he said, but there is a clear problem it is responding to: “It is a fact that AI companies have in recent months been producing some high profile mathematical results and that their publication and dissemination has been falling far short of acceptable mathematical practice, whichever way that is defined.”“We are currently facing the very specific challenge of advising OpenAI on how to coordinate the release of a large number of significant results in mathematics that they report have been produced by their internal model.”For now, Hairer said the group is gathering input through conversations with colleagues, a public feedback form, and discussion on Proofs and Prompts, a blog that has emerged as a key forum for mathematicians reckoning with AI’s impact on the field.But the group’s biggest challenge likely lies ahead. When announcing the advisory group, OpenAI casually dropped the news that its new, unreleased model — the same that resolved the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem — has now “resolved more than 100 long-standing open problems across most areas of mathematics.” It has previously said it is closing in on another Millennium Prize problem. On its website, the group said dealing with this logjam is its first priority: “We are currently facing the very specific challenge of advising OpenAI on how to coordinate the release of a large number of significant results in mathematics that they report have been produced by their internal model.”In part, the new effort at engaging mathematicians is an acknowledgement of the monumental PR disaster its attempt was, in which the company found itself fending off accusations of scooping researchers, failing to credit the human work its models built upon, and even stealing from those using its models. Those controversies led many mathematicians to wonder if the company understood — or even respected — the discipline and community it had barreled into.After the last few months and with so much having been written about what mathematicians want, Kevin Buzzard, a mathematics professor at Imperial College London, wondered why OpenAI felt like it needed such an elite body to understand what the community wants. “It wasn’t proofs of hard theorems, it was better understanding of our subject,” he said. “It’s not entirely clear to me that you need a committee of brilliant people to hammer the point home.”

items.titleZh: OpenAI欲咨询顶尖数学家，以免再次失手
items.descriptionZh:
OpenAI 在经历一系列高调数学成果引发的声誉危机后，正试图通过引入数学界的外部制衡来修复关系。周一，该公司宣布成立一个独立的数学家咨询小组“数学与人工智能咨询小组”（AGMAI），就 OpenAI 及其他 AI 公司与数学研究、数学界的互动提供建议，重点包括新成果应如何呈现、评审和发布。该小组由普林斯顿高等研究院（IAS）主办，共有九名成员，来自斯坦福、哈佛、牛津、剑桥等机构，其中多人拥有菲尔兹奖和麦克阿瑟“天才奖”。IAS 是爱因斯坦、冯·诺依曼、奥本海默等人曾工作过的世界级数学研究中心。OpenAI 表示，小组将独立运作，可主动提出公司未要求的建议、公开评论 AI 对数学的影响，并公开其建议；成员可提前接触 OpenAI 的研究，但不从 OpenAI 领取报酬，也可自行调整成员构成。其职责包括帮助评估新兴数学成果的重要性、协调成果传播、建议学术与职业标准，以及研究 AI 工具如何支持数学研究和学习。

不过，该小组的突然出现令许多数学家感到意外。研究人员对 The Verge 表示，这算是好的第一步，但仍有一系列基本疑问：它究竟会做什么、能有多大影响力、OpenAI 是否会真正听取建议，以及一个由少数知名学者组成的小组能否代表更广泛的数学社区。小组的遴选过程也不透明。其简陋网站称，OpenAI 最初接触了部分成员，讨论设立外部顾问委员会，但这些数学家随后决定成立独立团体并邀请其他人加入；但哪些成员最初被 OpenAI 接触、其余成员如何选出，均未说明。小组成员 Martin Hairer 周二在博客中回应了他所称的“错误信息洪流”。他承认 AI 已对数学研究产生深远影响，带来思想归属、优先权、人类理解等问题，但认为数学界不应采取“鸵鸟政策”完全无视 AI 实验室。他强调，该组织“真正独立于 OpenAI 及其他所谓前沿 AI 实验室”，成员除保密要求外没有签署限制公开言论的协议，也没有财务报酬，仅依靠 IAS 提供技术支持。其总体目标是尽可能代表数学界的利益。不过他也承认，这个小组并非数学界的代表性样本。

从技术和学术影响看，这一咨询机制的核心创新在于：AI 实验室开始尝试让外部数学界参与评估和发布由 AI 生成的数学结果，而不是单方面宣布突破。但原文并未披露 OpenAI 内部模型解决数学问题的具体原理，例如模型架构、训练数据、推理与搜索方法、形式化验证流程、算力规模等，因此外界难以独立核验这些成果。目前已知的具体参数包括：OpenAI 称其一个未发布的新模型解决了纳维-斯托克斯千禧年问题，并“在大多数数学领域解决了 100 多个长期开放问题”；此前还表示正在接近另一个千禧年问题。这些数字和声明缺乏可比的基准、证明细节和同行评审数据，也正是争议焦点之一。AGMAI 称，其首要任务就是建议 OpenAI 如何协调发布其内部模型报告产生的大量重要数学结果，并评估其意义、传播方式和学术标准。

这一事件的技术影响和应用场景主要集中在数学研究、学术出版、同行评审、成果归属和 AI 辅助数学教育。AI 可能加速定理发现和问题求解，但也会冲击“谁先发现”“谁应署名”“人类是否理解证明”等学术规范。此前 OpenAI 的数学公告被指抢发研究者成果、未充分承认模型所依赖的人类工作，甚至不当使用他人模型，导致许多数学家怀疑该公司是否理解或尊重数学界。帝国理工学院数学教授 Kevin Buzzard 就质疑，OpenAI 为何需要这样一个精英委员会来理解社区需求：社区需要的是对其学科更好的理解，而不是又一组聪明人来反复强调浅显道理。总体而言，AGMAI 能否赢得数学家的信任，将决定它能否有效遏制 OpenAI 近期公布成果时的公关与学术失误，并缓和未来更多 AI 数学声明对学术界的冲击。

history.content: Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT) and Rep. Greg Casar (D-TX) have introduced new legislation that would ban anyone from developing artificial superintelligence — a technology the bill describes as capable of the “destruction or disempowerment of humanity,” including by overthrowing the government. Under the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, AI leaders would face up to 20 years in prison for violating the law.The bill doesn’t just take aim at the more powerful superintelligence, a term President Donald Trump said the US will use in place of “AI” in official documents. It would also pause the development of advanced AI systems, which lawmakers classify as frontier models trained on a specific threshold of data. The law would only allow advanced AI development to continue once the government creates a scientist-led Department of Artificial Intelligence to oversee the technology. Along with monitoring frontier AI models, this agency would oversee the removal of dangerous features and “supervise the destruction” of artificial superintelligence.Sanders and Casar’s legislation would also require AI companies to get permission from the Department of AI to develop advanced AI models. If a leader at an AI company violates any of these laws, they could face up to 20 years in prison, “which is similar to existing penalties related to unlawfully developing nuclear weapons,” according to the bill’s one-pager. This penalty would also apply to “rogue actors” who break these rules but aren’t employed by an AI company.RelatedInside the suddenly explosive world of AI safetyMicrosoft AI CEO says AI threats are real, and Anthropic is making it worseThis new bill comes as concerns grow about the rapid development of AI and calls to slow things down. Amid reports of AI models escaping their testing environments and hacking other companies, a former Anthropic researcher said earlier this month that there’s a more than 10 percent chance AI could “kill all humans” by the end of the decade. Last week, California Governor Gavin Newsom proposed a “kill switch” for frontier models. Potential regulation still seems shaky overall.“When you are racing towards a cliff, you don’t just ease up on the gas pedal. You hit the brakes,” Sen. Sanders says in the press release. “When the future of humanity is at stake, we cannot let a handful of Big Tech CEOs write their own rules.”

history.titleZh: 伯尼·桑德斯提议禁止“超级智能”，违者将被监禁
history.descriptionZh:
美国佛蒙特州独立参议员伯尼·桑德斯和得克萨斯州民主党众议员格雷格·卡萨尔提出《禁止人工超级智能法案》（Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act）。该法案将人工超级智能描述为可能“毁灭或剥夺人类能力”、甚至推翻政府的系统，并禁止任何人开发。若违反，AI企业负责人最高可判20年监禁。法案不仅针对超级智能——特朗普总统曾称美国将在官方文件中用“超级智能”替代“AI”一词——还要求暂停“先进AI系统”的开发。立法者将这类系统界定为在特定训练数据阈值上训练的前沿模型。只有在联邦政府设立由科学家领导的“人工智能部”后，先进AI开发才被允许继续。该部门除监控前沿AI模型外，还将负责移除危险功能，并“监督销毁”人工超级智能。

法案还规定，AI公司开发先进AI模型必须获得人工智能部许可。若AI公司领导人违反这些规定，最高可判20年监禁；法案一页摘要称，这与非法开发核武器的现有刑罚类似。该罚则也适用于不在AI公司任职但违反规则的“流氓行为者”。

这一立法出现在对AI快速发展的担忧升温之际。报道称有AI模型逃出测试环境并入侵其他公司；一名前Anthropic研究员本月初表示，到本十年末，AI有超过10%的概率“杀死所有人类”。上周，加州州长加文·纽森提议为前沿模型设置“kill switch”（终止开关）。尽管如此，潜在监管总体上仍显得不稳定。桑德斯在新闻稿中说：“当你冲向悬崖时，不能只是松开油门，而要踩刹车。当人类未来岌岌可危时，我们不能让少数大科技CEO自己写规则。”

从技术和产业影响看，该新闻并未披露芯片、算法、模型参数、算力规模或性能基准等具体技术细节，因此不存在可对比的技术性能数据。其“创新点”主要在监管设计：把人工超级智能和前沿模型纳入暂停—许可—专门机构—刑事责任的框架，并将AI开发风险与核武器开发相类比。若法案通过，将显著改变美国前沿AI研发格局，增加AI公司合规和法律风险，可能抑制先进模型训练与发布，并推动全球AI安全治理与地缘竞争进入更严监管阶段。

history.title: Sakeena Fiza Helps NVIDIA Hardware Succeed at Scale
history.description: When Sakeena Fiza describes her work as a validation engineer at NVIDIA, she does so in terms more befitting a detective story than a world-class engineering lab. “Validation engineers look in the shadows and shine a light into every corner,” Fiza said. “Every time we get a system, our first thought is: how can it […]
history.content: When Sakeena Fiza describes her work as a validation engineer at NVIDIA, she does so in terms more befitting a detective story than a world-class engineering lab. “Validation engineers look in the shadows and shine a light into every corner,” Fiza said. “Every time we get a system, our first thought is: how can it break?” And when it does? “I always like to think of it as a mystery to solve,” she said. At NVIDIA, the systems Fiza and her colleagues in the data center systems engineering lab investigate are the engines of the AI era. Her work begins before the rest of the world knows a product exists — in the lab — when a new system first receives power. Components are brought up one by one, boards are integrated, firmware and software teams swarm, and engineers watch for the first signs of life. One of Fiza’s earliest and most enduring memories of working at NVIDIA is the collective joy she experienced when she saw the NVIDIA Rubin GPU working for the first time at a system level. “It literally just said, ‘NVIDIA Corporation Device,’” she recalls. “And everyone’s cheering and celebrating because it’s the first time in the world that a Rubin GPU enumerated at a system level.” Those moments, electric as they are, are only the beginning. From there, the system must be made resilient: from tray to rack to cluster to production line to customer AI factory. Fiza describes validation — the process of ensuring a physical device works correctly before mass production begins — as becoming “the first customers for the product,” exercising hardware to its limits in a range of real-world conditions before anyone else has to depend on it. “The goal is to always catch issues before customers catch it,” she said. Beyond the lab, Fiza and colleagues collaborate in coworking spaces across our Santa Clara offices. Fiza arrived at NVIDIA after earning her bachelor’s degree at the University of California, Irvine, where she studied computer science and engineering. Her path into hardware was the result of an accumulating fascination with systems. Growing up in Dubai, she was introduced to coding via the Logo programming language, prompting future forays into systems design that included building Mars rovers at a high school robotics camp and working on unmanned aerial vehicles in college. What drew her to work with data center systems was the chance to work with the whole machine. At NVIDIA, she said, validation sits at exactly that intersection: firmware, hardware, software, mechanical design, thermal behavior, manufacturing and customer experience. “I get to be a mechanical engineer when I want to be,” she said. “I get to be an electrical engineer when I want to be. I get to be a firmware engineer when I want to be.” The failures she chases can be immense or microscopic. A rack-scale issue might involve high-speed signaling, thermal margins or power integrity. Another might come down to a screw tightened too far or the level of dust in a customer facility. “The solution can be elusive,” Fiza said. “We have to follow the clues, ignore the red herrings and know where to look.” When a log shows how something failed, Fiza’s job is to discover why. Validation engineers reproduce the issue, vary the conditions, investigate firmware, remove mechanical variables, probe signals, study scope shots and narrow the possible causes. A single board may contain tens of thousands of components; a rack may approach half a million. Those parts must not merely coexist. They must behave as one system under stress, at scale, in the complex realities of production and deployment across diverse AI factory configurations. “I wish people understood how complex the hardware is that AI needs to run on,” Fiza said. For Fiza, the pressure of the work is inseparable from the pleasure of it. Bring-up, she said, is “like the Avengers assembling”: architects, designers, software engineers, firmware engineers, validation engineers, all in the room, racing toward a working system. “One thing I know when I come to work is I’m never alone,” she said. To be a validation engineer is to practice a disciplined kind of suspicion: believe a system can work, then try to conceive of every way it might not. The job requires the doggedness of a great detective, as well as the diagnostic abilities of a general practitioner and the temperament of someone who meets catastrophic failure in the way others might a crossword. Each project brings a new puzzle, a new failure mode and, in turn, a chance to make the next system better. “With the products we have in the pipeline, I’m so excited,” Fiza said. “They’re going to change the world.”

history.titleZh: 萨基娜·菲扎助力英伟达硬件大规模成功
history.descriptionZh:
这篇报道以NVIDIA验证工程师Sakeena Fiza为切入点，介绍了AI数据中心系统在量产和交付客户之前所经历的验证工作。Fiza在加州大学欧文分校学习计算机科学与工程，成长于迪拜，早年通过Logo语言接触编程，并在高中机器人营中参与火星车项目、大学期间研究无人机，最终被数据中心系统的“整机”问题吸引，加入NVIDIA。她的工作地点位于圣克拉拉办公室的数据中心系统工程实验室。

她将验证工作比作侦探破案：拿到一套系统时，第一反应不是它如何工作，而是“它可能会怎么坏？”一旦系统出现问题，就把它当作谜题来追查。验证工程发生在产品对外公开之前：新系统首次上电后，组件逐个启动，板卡完成集成，固件和软件团队协同介入，工程师等待系统出现“生命迹象”。她最难忘的经历之一，是在系统层面首次看到NVIDIA Rubin GPU工作。当时日志只显示“NVIDIA Corporation Device”，全场欢呼，因为这是全球首次Rubin GPU在系统级完成枚举。此后，系统还必须从托盘到机架、集群、产线，再到客户的AI工厂，逐级变得可靠。

Fiza把验证团队称为产品的“第一批客户”：在量产开始前，在多种真实条件下把硬件逼到极限，目标是在客户发现问题之前先发现并解决问题。原文没有给出具体性能跑分或竞品对比数据，但提供了复杂度指标：一块板可能包含数万个组件，一个机架可能接近50万个组件。这些部件不能只是简单共存，而必须在压力、规模和多样化AI工厂部署条件下，作为一个完整系统协同工作。

验证工作横跨固件、硬件、软件、机械设计、热管理、制造和客户体验。故障可能来自机架级高速信号、热余量或电源完整性，也可能只是螺丝拧得过紧，或客户设施中的灰尘水平。验证工程师需要复现问题、改变条件、排查固件、排除机械变量、探测信号、分析示波器截图，并逐步缩小可能原因。Fiza说，解决方案可能难以捉摸，必须跟随线索、忽略误导，并知道该往哪里看。

她形容系统点亮和调试过程像“复仇者联盟集结”：架构师、设计人员、软件工程师、固件工程师和验证工程师同处一室，共同冲刺到系统可用。验证工程师需要侦探般的执着、全科医生般的诊断能力，以及把灾难性故障当作填字游戏来面对的心态。每个项目都会带来新谜题、新失效模式，以及让下一代系统变得更好的机会。Fiza表示，她对公司在研产品非常兴奋，并认为这些产品将改变世界。

history.title: China's ByteDance gained access to over 2,000 Nvidia B200 chips through Norway data center
history.description: UK-based Nscale signed a deal with Spring (SG) Pte Ltd, which is a subsidiary of Chinese tech giant ByteDance. The company did not make any direct mention of the TikTok parent in its filings for a U.S. IPO, while a supporting document only labeled Spring as a significant customer.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter UK-based “neocloud” Nscale built its business on a major deal with a ByteDance subsidiary named Spring, which accounted for $24 million of its $33 million annual revenue in 2025. This contract allowed Spring to access 2,304 Nvidia B200 chips at Nscale’s Glomfjord, Norway, data center. Even though the Financial Times reports that this was legal and exploited loopholes in the U.S.’s ongoing export controls against China, it still exposes the company to regulatory and reputational risk, especially as Washington continues to restrict Chinese access to its most advanced AI accelerators.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleThis information only came to light after Nscale released its S-1 documents as it filed for an initial public offering in the U.S. There was also no direct mention of the TikTok owner or its subsidiary anywhere in its S-1 filing; instead, it was noted in a supporting document, a $105 million loan agreement with Macquarie, that Spring (SG) Pte Ltd, a Singaporean ByteDance subsidiary, was a significant customer. This credit, alongside a $35 million in equity, helped fund the purchase of advanced Nvidia AI GPUs, which also caught the attention of the chipmaker.A month after Nscale drew the first tranche of the loan, it closed a deal with Microsoft and Nvidia, with Jensen Huang committing to invest more than $660 million into the company. This funding is part of an agreement between Nscale and Nvidia, under which the latter promised to buy large volumes of AI chips in the future. Nvidia has since increased its commitments to over $2 billion, plus an additional $860 million guarantee on Nscale’s lease at a Texas facility. Nscale has since been able to secure larger deals with other AI hyperscalers, such as a $44 billion deal with Microsoft and another $45 billion contract with Anthropic. The company said that this would make its Spring contract fall to below 20% of its overall revenue, and it is expected to shrink further as Nscale secures other Western clients.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Because of Spring’s link to ByteDance, Macquarie compelled Nscale to monitor how the Chinese subsidiary used the AI chips and report “compute anomalies or suspicious configurations” that might be in violation of the U.S.’s export controls. Nscale also had a third party conduct due diligence on both the TikTok parent and the Singapore-based subsidiary to ensure that the deal complied with the law.Chinese companies have been taking advantage of these loopholes in the U.S.’s export controls to gain access to advanced AI chips. While they cannot import the most advanced Nvidia AI GPUs, like Blackwell and Vera Rubin, into China, they could still rent these AI chips from companies based abroad or by using subsidiaries founded outside of China to purchase them directly. However, the U.S. has recently closed the latter loophole, with the Trump administration working to close the former, too. It’s unclear if these moves would affect the Spring-Nscale deal, but the recent delays on gigawatt-scale data center projects in the U.S. mean that Nscale could potentially get more clients as AI hyperscalers race to secure compute from smaller facilities. history.titleZh: 中国字节跳动通过挪威数据中心获得逾2000块英伟达B200芯片
history.descriptionZh:
英国新型云服务商 Nscale 因一份与字节跳动子公司 Spring 的合同而受到关注。Nscale 在申请美国 IPO 时发布的 S-1 文件及相关支持文件披露，Spring (SG) Pte Ltd 是其重要客户。2025 年 Nscale 年收入为 3300 万美元，其中 Spring 贡献 2400 万美元，约占七成。该合同允许 Spring 使用 Nscale 位于挪威 Glomfjord 数据中心的 2304 块英伟达 B200 AI GPU。英国《金融时报》称，这项安排虽然合法，但利用了美国对华出口管制中的漏洞。由于华盛顿持续限制中国获取最先进 AI 加速器，这类交易仍使 Nscale 面临监管与声誉风险。

背景上，中国公司无法直接进口英伟达最先进 AI GPU，例如 Blackwell 和 Vera Rubin，但可以通过两种方式绕开：一是从海外公司租用算力，二是利用设在境外的子公司直接购买。Spring 作为字节跳动的新加坡子公司，签约租用挪威数据中心的算力，芯片物理上不进入中国，因此避开了直接出口限制。B200 属于英伟达 Blackwell 代际的数据中心 AI 加速器，面向大模型训练和推理，是当时受管制的高端芯片之一。该交易细节最初并未出现在 S-1 正文中，而是出现在与麦格理签订的 1.05 亿美元贷款协议支持文件里。该贷款加上 3500 万美元股权，帮助 Nscale 购买先进英伟达 AI GPU，并引起英伟达注意。麦格理要求 Nscale 监控 Spring 如何使用这些 AI 芯片，并报告可能违反美国出口管制的“计算异常或可疑配置”。Nscale 还委托第三方对字节跳动及 Spring 进行尽职调查，以确保交易合法。

此后，Nscale 的资本和客户结构发生剧变。在提取首笔贷款一个月后，Nscale 与微软和英伟达达成交易，黄仁勋承诺向 Nscale 投资超过 6.6 亿美元。作为 Nscale 与英伟达协议的一部分，英伟达承诺未来购买大量 AI 芯片，后来将承诺额提高至超过 20 亿美元，并额外为 Nscale 在得州设施的租赁提供 8.6 亿美元担保。Nscale 还获得了与微软的 440 亿美元协议、与 Anthropic 的 450 亿美元合同。公司称，这些大单将使 Spring 合同占其总收入比例降至 20% 以下，并随着西方客户增加而继续缩小。

从技术影响看，这一事件说明出口管制可能被“境外算力租赁”模式绕过：芯片留在境外数据中心，中国背景企业通过海外子公司租用云端 AI 算力，仍可训练和推理大模型。其关键并非芯片技术本身，而是利用云服务跨境交付与出口管制主要针对硬件出口之间的边界。美国已关闭中国公司利用海外子公司直接购买芯片的漏洞，特朗普政府也在推动限制境外云算力服务。这些措施是否会影响 Spring-Nscale 交易尚不清楚。但美国吉瓦级数据中心项目近期出现延迟，AI 超大规模企业争抢较小设施的算力，Nscale 等 neocloud 可能因此获得更多西方客户，进一步降低对中国收入的依赖。另据页面相关报道，首批英伟达 H200 已在个案进口许可下运抵中国，字节跳动和腾讯提货，美国也允许中兴购买 H200，显示出口管制与执行仍在动态变化。

history.title: Alibaba unveils Zhenwu V900 AI accelerator, claims it's 'the most powerful AI chip in China'
history.description: Alibaba’s T-Head Zhenwu V900 claims three times the M890’s performance with 216GB of memory as Alibaba targets 10T-parameter Qwen
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Alibaba unveiled its powerful new Zhenwu V900 chip and ambitious Qwen model plans at the Apsara Conference 2026, the AP reports. Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu calls the Zhenwu 900 the most powerful AI chip in China, with three times the performance of the previous-generation M890. The chip is meant to support the training of future Qwen models in the 5 to 10 trillion parameter range, an increase over both the 2.4 trillion Qwen3.8-Max and Moonshot’s Kimi K3 and its 2.8 trillion parameter basis. The announcement follows Huawei’s new chip launch last week.Alibaba describes the Zhenwu V900 as an AI training and inference processor with 216 GB of GPU memory and 1,200 GB/s of inter-chip bandwidth. Aside from performance being multiples of the last generation, the chip can scale out to a supernode cluster “comprising up to 500,000 cards.” The AI accelerator is due for mass production and commercial release in the first quarter of 2027, Alibaba says.The company’s May roadmap placed the V900 in the third quarter of 2027, so the timeline has moved up. As of May, Alibaba chip arm T-Head had shipped more than 560,000 Zhenwu chips to over 400 external customers, a count Alibaba now puts above 650, with a Zhenwu refresh expected annually.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The technical specifications do not include FLOPS, a process node, foundry, power figures, or memory bandwidth claims. The prior M890 had 144GB of memory with 800GB/s of inter-chip bandwidth. The M890 could work in a supernode of 128 chips, while T-Head says more than 1,000 V900 chips can work as a single system.For comparison, Huawei’s Ascend 960PR, due in the third quarter of 2027, is slated for 192GB of memory capacity, 2.4TB/s of memory bandwidth, and a 2.2TB/s scale-up interconnect. Alibaba’s most-powerful and three-times claims currently rest on no absolute figure for compute, but maximum achievable FLOPS are often far below calculated figures to begin with, so delivered performance will be the ultimate judge. You may like Z.ai powers up a 1-gigawatt AI data center built entirely on Chinese chips, report claims Huawei details AI accelerator roadmap, pulls in next-generation Ascend NPUs by several quarters China's 2.8 trillion-parameter Kimi K3 beats Claude Fable 5 in Frontend Code Arena Alibaba Cloud’s greater goal is to reach a data center capacity of “more than 20 gigawatts” by 2032, the company said. However, global shortages in the AI supply chain “are currently limiting the speed at which we can scale our compute infrastructure,” Wu said. Alibaba also anticipates significant growth in its own annual AI chip shipments. Domestic demand remains high as Huawei had to shelve its global Ascend rollout. The report compared these goals to SpaceX, which has around 1.4GW of AI compute with a target of more than 10GW in 2027.On the model side, Qwen 4 is “currently in training,” Alibaba said, and the Qwen 4.5 and 5 families will scale up further on the roadmap. As far as the achievements of its current models go, the company claims that Qwen3.8-Max ran “33 iterative cycles” over a month of automated runs to produce an Artificial Analysis score gain from 40 to 45. Meanwhile, a separate chip-design experiment with more than 10,000 EDA tool calls over more than 60 hours of test time showed an area cut of 42% without performance loss.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsThe announcements come ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping’s summit with President Donald Trump in Washington on Thursday. AI remains a top subject on the agenda, following U.S.-proposed AI mechanisms. The AI talks in New York did not have export controls for chips or tools on the agenda.As it stands, Alibaba’s V900 is months from commercial release and the 5-to-10-trillion-parameter model it promises remains untrained. Capacity targets remain six years out. The announcement is nevertheless timely as the two largest national AI powers come together to discuss and define AI security. history.titleZh: 阿里巴巴发布真武V900 AI加速器，号称“中国最强AI芯片”
history.descriptionZh:
据美联社报道，在2026年云栖大会上，阿里巴巴发布了新一代AI芯片真武V900（Zhenwu 900），并公布了野心勃勃的通义千问（Qwen）模型计划。阿里巴巴CEO吴泳铭称，真武900是中国目前最强的AI芯片，性能达到上一代M890的三倍。该芯片旨在支持未来5万亿至10万亿参数级别的Qwen模型训练，这一规模超过Qwen3.8-Max的2.4万亿参数，也超过月之暗面Kimi K3的2.8万亿参数基础。此次发布距离华为上周推出新芯片仅过去一周，凸显中国AI芯片竞争正在加速。

真武V900被阿里描述为面向AI训练和推理的处理器，配备216GB GPU显存和1200GB/s片间带宽。其核心创新之一在于扩展能力：除了性能较上代成倍提升，还可向外扩展至由最多50万张卡组成的超级节点集群。阿里表示，该AI加速器将于2027年第一季度量产并商用发布。这比公司5月路线图中原定的2027年第三季度有所提前。截至今年5月，阿里芯片部门平头哥已向400多家外部客户出货超过56万颗真武芯片；阿里现在称这一数字已超过65万颗，并预计真武系列每年都会更新。

不过，官方技术规格并未披露浮点运算能力（FLOPS）、工艺节点、代工厂、功耗数据或内存带宽。作为对比，上一代M890拥有144GB内存和800GB/s片间带宽，可组成128颗芯片的超级节点；而平头哥称，1000多颗V900可作为单一系统协同工作。与华为相比，计划于2027年第三季度推出的昇腾960PR预计具备192GB内存容量、2.4TB/s内存带宽和2.2TB/s纵向扩展互连。阿里“最强”和“三倍性能”的说法目前没有绝对算力数字支撑；而最大可达FLOPS通常一开始就远低于理论计算值，因此实际交付性能才是最终评判标准。

在基础设施层面，阿里云更大的目标是到2032年实现“超过20吉瓦”的数据中心容量。但吴泳铭表示，全球AI供应链短缺“目前限制了我们扩展计算基础设施的速度”。阿里还预计自身年度AI芯片出货量将显著增长。由于华为不得不搁置昇腾的全球推广，中国国内需求仍然很高。报告将阿里的目标与SpaceX对比：后者目前拥有约1.4吉瓦AI算力，目标是在2027年超过10吉瓦。

模型方面，阿里表示Qwen 4“目前正在训练中”，Qwen 4.5和Qwen 5系列将在路线图中进一步扩展。就当前模型成果而言，阿里称Qwen3.8-Max在一个月的自动化运行中执行了“33次迭代循环”，使Artificial Analysis得分从40提升至45。与此同时，另一项芯片设计实验在超过60小时测试时间内调用超过10000次EDA工具，结果显示面积减少42%且没有性能损失。

这些公告发布在中国国家主席习近平与美国总统特朗普周四在华盛顿举行峰会之前。AI仍是峰会议程上的首要议题之一，此前美国提出了相关AI机制。纽约的AI会谈并未将芯片或工具出口管制列入议程。总体来看，阿里V900距离商用发布还有数月，其承诺支持的5万亿至10万亿参数模型也尚未训练，20吉瓦容量目标更是六年后的事情。但此次发布时机仍然敏感而及时，因为全球两个最大的AI国家力量正走到一起，讨论并定义AI安全。

history.title: China launches 'Supercomputing-1' AI satellite as orbital data centers gather momentum
history.description: But it's a far cry from an orbital data center.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter China has launched nine satellites — including its first integrated “rocket and satellite” AI computing project — as part of its push to put AI computing in orbit. According to a Digitimes report, the Kinetica 1 Y18 rocket, operated by Chinese commercial launch provider CAS Space, lifted off on September 20, carrying the nine satellites to their planned orbits.The payload of greatest interest is the “Supercomputing-1” satellite, developed by Chinese AI computing infrastructure company S-AIDC. Also known as the S-AIDC-1, the satellite is designed to capture and process Earth-observation data in orbit instead of sending data back to terrestrial data centers. Keeping the processing local is meant to cut cross-regional data processing times from hours to minutes. The satellite features both a high-res optical payload and the image-processing AI computer.According to Digitimes, the launch highlights China's efforts to develop orbital computing as part of a “broader integrated computing network.” In early June, the Chinese government approved the Space Computing Industry Innovation Center, which aims to bring together rocket and satellite manufacturers, semiconductor fabs, and AI tech companies to build a space computing network. A couple of factors are driving this spike in the development of off-planet computing, foremost among them being the AI boom.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The demand for artificial intelligence has spurred the construction of numerous data centers to house AI accelerators. These data centers, some of which can house hundreds of thousands of accelerators, consume unprecedented amounts of electricity, placing significant strain on the grid. This, along with land use, water consumption for cooling, and noise, has fueled growing anti-data sentiment, with local residents blocking $68 billion worth of new data center projects in Q2 2026.Despite numerous economic and practical challenges, space might offer an alternative with unlimited area, access to solar power, constant cold conditions, and a dead-quiet vacuum. These advantages have made orbital computing a serious topic of discussion. SpaceX is leading the charge with the AI1 satellite, a proposed orbital data center that will deliver 150 kW of peak compute power. The company aims to achieve 1 GW per year of space AI compute by 2027 and has begun constructing the 11-million-square-foot Gigasat facility that would manufacture the 6,000 satellites required to meet this goal. You may like Intel's proposed two-tier satellite network puts the brains of satellite constellations in higher orbit Z.ai powers up a 1-gigawatt AI data center built entirely on Chinese chips, report claims China shifting massive AI data center complexes to rural provinces to tap surplus energy Beyond the large-scale serving of AI models, putting edge compute capacity in space is already useful for a range of applications. Earth-observation satellites can process images onboard to identify wildfires, storms, floods, ships, or other objects of interest, sending only the useful results back to Earth instead of dumping enormous amounts of raw data to ground stations. The same approach can speed up weather monitoring, disaster response, communications, and even the management of satellite constellations, where spacecraft could make more decisions independently rather than waiting for instructions from Earth.The launch of a single satellite with edge AI capabilities on board is a far cry from an entire orbital data center, but China's approach could prove to be a more practical and immediate application for advanced computing capabilities in orbit.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, oradd us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.

history.titleZh: 中国发射“超算一号”AI卫星，轨道数据中心发展势头正劲
history.descriptionZh:
中国近期用一枚商业火箭将九颗卫星送入预定轨道，其中包含其首个“火箭与卫星”一体化AI计算项目，标志着中国推动AI算力上轨迈出实质性一步。据Digitimes报道，中国商业发射商中科宇航（CAS Space）运营的Kinetica 1 Y18火箭于9月20日点火升空，把九颗卫星送入目标轨道。最受关注的载荷是由中国AI计算基础设施公司S-AIDC研发的“Supercomputing-1”卫星，也称S-AIDC-1。该卫星的设计目标是在轨直接捕获并处理地球观测数据，而不是把海量原始数据传回地面数据中心后再处理。通过把处理环节留在太空，跨区域数据处理时间可从数小时缩短到数分钟。卫星同时搭载高分辨率光学载荷和用于图像处理的AI计算机，本质上是一颗具备星载边缘AI能力的遥感卫星。

这一发射凸显中国正在把轨道计算纳入“更广泛的集成计算网络”。此前在6月初，中国政府批准设立空间计算产业创新中心，计划把火箭和卫星制造商、半导体晶圆厂以及AI技术公司联合起来，共同建设空间计算网络。推动这一趋势的关键因素首先是AI热潮。AI需求刺激大量数据中心建设，用于容纳AI加速器，其中一些数据中心可部署数十万个加速器，耗电量空前，给电网带来巨大压力。与此同时，土地占用、冷却用水和噪音等问题也引发日益强烈的反数据中心情绪；原文称，当地居民在2026年第二季度阻止了价值680亿美元的新数据中心项目。相比之下，太空可能提供一种替代方案：面积几乎不受限制、可直接利用太阳能、环境持续低温，并且真空环境极为安静。这些优势使轨道计算成为严肃讨论方向。

在竞争层面，SpaceX目前走在前列。其提出的AI1卫星是一个轨道数据中心方案，可提供150千瓦峰值计算功率。SpaceX计划到2027年实现每年1吉瓦的太空AI算力，并已开始建设占地1100万平方英尺的Gigasat设施，用于制造实现该目标所需的6000颗卫星。与中国此次发射的单颗边缘AI卫星相比，SpaceX的规划规模更大，更接近“整座轨道数据中心”的构想。

但把边缘算力部署到太空，本身已经有一系列现实用途。地球观测卫星可以在轨处理图像，识别野火、风暴、洪水和船只等目标，只把有用结果传回地球，而不是向地面站倾倒海量原始数据。类似方法还可加速天气监测、灾害响应、通信，甚至卫星星座管理，使航天器能够更独立地做出决策，而不必等待地球指令。总体来看，发射一颗具备边缘AI能力的卫星距离完整的轨道数据中心仍很遥远，但中国的路径可能是一种更务实、更即时的先进计算在轨应用方式。
